citation.title: Learning topology optimization process via convolutional long-short-term memory autoencoder-decoder
citation.authors: Qiaochu Ma; Edward C. DeMeter; Saurabh Basu
citation.venue: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering, 124(11), 2571–2588

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On the test set, the ConvLSTM model reduced average computation time from 3.711 s for SIMP to 0.001 s while reporting a 5.13% average compliance error for connected predictions.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 4.1 gives 3.711 s average for the conventional method and 0.001 s for the proposed method; 3.711 / 0.001 = 3711.
claim.alternatives: Abstract claims reduced cost for unseen boundary/load conditions; Table 2 reports up to 99.99% saved at 80 × 80.

baseline.implementation: Topy open-source 2D/3D SIMP solver for training data; paper's test implementation in Python
baseline.hardware_classical: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 3090 GPU used for experiments; separate classical hardware not specified
baseline.training_time: Reported graphically for mesh-size/hidden-dimension combinations in Figure 11; no single numeric value in text
baseline.data_generation_cost: 5,000 train + 100 validation + 100 test samples at default configuration; generation time not stated (Section 4)
baseline.quality_metric: pixel error and compliance error against SIMP; Table 1
baseline.quality_gap: 5.13% average compliance error, with two disconnected cases excluded from the average (Section 4.1, Table 1)

R1.evidence: Section 4.1, Table 1 compares SIMP and predictions on the same test conditions and reports 5.13% mean compliance error; unsure whether this exactly meets the protocol's volume condition, so pass by convention.

R2.evidence: Sections 4.1–4.3 report SIMP timing and a shared GTX 3090 experiment platform, but do not establish any R2 inefficiency criterion.

R3.evidence: Section 4 and Figure 11 report training sample counts and training time, while training-data generation time and amortized break-even are absent.

R4.evidence: Section 4.1 reports compliance errors and identifies two disconnected predictions among 100 tests, but excludes them from the mean and does not report constraint-violation rates.

reporting.n_test_cases: 100 in the default test set; Section 4

notes: Two disconnected cases with large compliance errors are excluded from the average reported in Table 1.
